properties.name: WHAT WORKED, re-measured on 0.77.0 (2026-10-02): the reporter's bulk pattern round-trips through --call. import_graph one document, export_graph, then compare_designs with base_path set to that export reads identical: true (110 nodes and 140 edges unchanged, 0.12 s). Do not regress it
properties.statement:
From "Working patterns that pay off" in art:vscode-call-door-field-report-2026-10-02: "Bulk work goes through one document ... import_graph it once, export_graph, then compare_designs with base_path set to the export: it should read identical." Measured once by triage agent D on a scratch design (0.77.0; outputs triage-D/out/import_hand110.stdout, export_110_first.stdout, compare_110.stdout).

- import_graph {path: hand-110.json} into an empty store: exit 0; 110 nodes and 140 edges written, none skipped.
- export_graph {path: exp110.json}: exit 0; content_hash sha256:99a78218…85f0.
- compare_designs {base_path: exp110.json}: exit 0, 0.12 s. other "live graph", ancestry "unknown". summary.identical true, nodes_unchanged 110, edges_unchanged 140; every added, changed and removed count is 0.

HOLDS. The round trip is the cheapest whole-design check a door agent has after a bulk write. It compares the live store with what it just exported, so it proves the export is faithful. It does not prove the import matched the source document; for that, compare against the source document itself.
